correctness.rationale: The exact integral 12-component XR equation from the originating source was reconstructed. The 21 explicit points satisfy an exhaustive incidence census of 9 ordinary sixfold and 12 ordinary double points; all 66 component pairs saturate their Bezout degrees. The six Hessians have determinant (-2,-6,-2,-2,-6,-6). Exhaustive exact 210 cross-point, 174 excluded-incidence and 147 gradient-transversality tests have nonzero norm-gcd obstructions supported only at 2 and 3. Thus every p>=5 preserves distinct smooth components and the full 21-point incidence. Elementary quadratic Galois action yields exact rational counts 21,13,9,13 by p mod 12, and Dirichlet gives densities. Standalone Python3 verifier replayed; twelve finite-prime enumerations are consistency checks, not the proof of universality.

value.rationale: XR is a distinguished degree-18 free conic–line arrangement with nine sixfold points, whose singular-point arithmetic is not determined by its published geometric incidence. The result completely classifies the smallest common singular splitting field, seven quadratic Galois pairs, and all prime-field rational singular counts, while proving no bad primes >=5 for its fixed integral presentation by a finite exact obstruction census. This is a natural complete arithmetic invariant useful for comparison of reductions and their rational incidence schemes, not a random narrow slice; limitations include p=2,3 and positive-characteristic freeness.
